summary: This work introduces heterogeneous quantum error-correcting codes where distinct qubit types with different error rates or noise biases are strategically placed within Clifford-deformed surface codes and studies their performance using tensor network decoding. For qubits with identical bias but different error rates, placing noisier qubits in the bulk (high syndrome multiplicity) yields thresholds exceeding 0.4 with exponential improvements in logical error rate; for qubits with identical error rates but different biases, the optimal strategy reverses, placing high-bias qubits on the boundary and increasing thresholds from 0.29 to 0.40 at $\eta_{\mathrm{high}} = 1000$.
motivation: Heterogeneous qubit systems are increasingly common across quantum platforms—trapped ions use different atomic species, transmons have fabrication-induced $T_1$ and $T_2$ variation, and hybrid processors mix weakly biased and strongly biased ($\eta > 100$) qubits—yet prior work has only considered homogeneous error models.
method: Heterogeneous codes composed of two qubit types were studied in two regimes isolated via code-capacity analysis: (1) same bias $\eta \in \{10, 100\}$ but error rates differing by factor 10, and (2) same error rate but biases $\eta_{\mathrm{low}} = 10$ and $\eta_{\mathrm{high}} \in \{100, 1000\}$. Maximum-likelihood tensor network decoding with bond dimension $\chi = 16$ and critical exponent fitting on distances $d = 5, 7, 9$ determined thresholds; a stabilizer-ratio hypothesis (ratio of bulk to boundary stabilizer touches) was proposed to unify both placement rules.
result: Regime A (same bias, different rates): placing noisy qubits in bulk achieves $p_{\mathrm{th}} > 0.4$ versus $p_{\mathrm{th}} \approx 0.2$ for boundary placement, with the logical error rate ratio exceeding $10^3$ at $d=9$ and $\eta=100$. Regime B (same rate, different bias): placing high-bias qubits on boundary increases threshold from 0.292(5) to 0.360(9) at $\eta_{\mathrm{high}}=100$ and from 0.29(1) to 0.398(4) at $\eta_{\mathrm{high}}=1000$. The logical channel exhibits bias inversion despite $Z$-biased physical noise, with $\eta_L \approx 4 \times 10^{-3}$.
